# How to Maximize Sales on Small Business Saturday: A Holiday Marketing Checklist


[Try Thryv for Free](https://www.thryv.com/marketingcentertrial/?utm_medium=OrganicSocial&utm_source=blog)


By[Rebecca Riserbato](https://www.thryv.com/blog/author/rebeccawhite/) , Small Business Expert

Key Takeaways


##


1. Improve your online visibility: Update your website, business listings, and Google Business Profile so customers can find you during holiday searches.
2. Create compelling holiday offers: Use gift cards, service packages, bundles, and exclusive promotions to give customers a reason to shop small.
3. Make social media work harder: Use short-form videos, customer testimonials, and seasonal content to reach more local shoppers.
4. Build customer trust: Collect and showcase reviews to help potential customers feel confident choosing your business.
5. Personalize your marketing: Use email and text campaigns to share relevant offers, reminders, and seasonal updates.
6. Make buying easy: Simplify your website, booking process, and payment options to turn more interest into sales.
7. Keep customers coming back: Follow up after Small Business Saturday to encourage repeat visits and purchases throughout the holidays.


Small Business Saturday is more than just a shopping day. It’s an opportunity for local businesses to attract new customers, strengthen community relationships, and build momentum for the holiday season.


But standing out during the holidays takes more than offering a seasonal discount. Customers are discovering businesses through online searches, social media, customer reviews, and even AI-powered recommendations. To compete, small businesses need a marketing strategy that makes it easy for customers to find them, trust them, and choose them.


Whether you own a retail shop, restaurant, salon, or home service business, the right holiday marketing strategies can help you attract more customers and maximize seasonal sales.


This Small Business Saturday marketing checklist covers seven ways to improve your online visibility, promote holiday offers, connect with customers, and turn seasonal shoppers into repeat customers.

### 1. Optimize Your Online Presence for Holiday Searches


Before customers visit your business, they need to find you. And during the holiday season, they’re searching for everything from local gift ideas and seasonal promotions to nearby services and last-minute appointments.


Start by[reviewing your online presence](https://www.thryv.com/blog/optimize-website-for-featured-snippets-ai-answers/) to make sure customers can find accurate, up-to-date information wherever they’re searching.


Here are a few ways to improve your holiday visibility:


- **Update your Google Business Profile:** Confirm your holiday hours, address, phone number and website. Add recent photos, seasonal updates and relevant offers.


- **Refresh your online listings:** Check that your business information is consistent across Google, Yelp, Facebook, and other directories.


- **Update your website:** Add holiday promotions, gift options, seasonal services, and clear calls to action so visitors know what to do next.


- **Use relevant local keywords:** Incorporate phrases customers might search for, such as “holiday gifts near me,” “local holiday shopping,” or “holiday home cleaning services.”


- **Make your content easy for AI search to understand:** Clearly explain what your business offers, where you operate, who you serve, and what makes your products or services valuable.


AI-powered search is becoming another way consumers discover businesses. Clear website content, accurate business information, and helpful customer reviews can make it easier for search engines and AI tools to understand your business.

### 2. Create Holiday Promotions Customers Actually Want


Holiday shoppers have plenty of options, so your[promotions](https://www.thryv.com/blog/12-days-of-holiday-marketing-ideas/) need to give them a reason to choose your business.


While discounts can attract attention, you don’t have to compete with big retailers on price. Focus on offers that highlight the value, convenience, and personal experience your business provides.


Consider these Small Business Saturday marketing ideas:


- **Create holiday bundles:** Combine popular products or services into a convenient package at a special price.


- **Offer gift cards:** Make it easy for customers to purchase gifts for friends and family, even when they aren’t sure what to choose.


- **Introduce seasonal packages:** Promote limited-time services, holiday appointments or special product collections.


- **Reward loyal customers:** Give returning customers early access to promotions, exclusive offers, or complimentary add-ons.


- **Offer a shopping experience:** Consider complimentary gift wrapping, product demonstrations, seasonal events, or personalized recommendations.


For service-based businesses, think about how customers can give your services as gifts. A salon could offer a holiday beauty package, while a home service business could promote seasonal maintenance or giftable service certificates.


The goal is to create an offer that feels valuable to customers while still supporting your business goals.


### 3. Use Social Media and Short-Form Video to Drive Discovery


Social media is one of the easiest ways to introduce your business to new customers and keep existing ones engaged throughout the holidays.


But simply posting a holiday graphic or announcing a discount isn’t always enough. Customers want to see what makes your business different and what they can expect when they shop with you.


[Short-form videos](https://www.thryv.com/blog/short-form-video-content-local-brands/) , product demonstrations, and behind-the-scenes content can help bring your business to life.


Try these social media ideas:


- **Showcase holiday products or services:** Create short videos highlighting gift ideas, seasonal packages, popular services, or customer favorites.


- **Share behind-the-scenes content:** Show how your team prepares for the holidays, packages orders, or gets ready for a busy season.


- **Create gift guides:** Put together gift recommendations based on different interests, budgets, or recipients.


- **Feature customer experiences:** Share customer testimonials, photos, and user-generated content (with permission).


- **Build anticipation:** Use countdowns, Stories, and promotional previews to remind followers about upcoming Small Business Saturday deals.


- **Partner with local creators:** Work with community influencers or complementary businesses to introduce your brand to new audiences.


You don’t need a professional video production team to make this work. A smartphone, good lighting, and a clear message are often enough to create engaging content.


Remember to include your location, website, or a clear next step in your posts so interested customers know how to find you.

### 4. Build Trust With Customer Reviews and Social Proof


Holiday shoppers want to feel confident about where they’re spending their money. Before visiting a business, booking an appointment, or making a purchase, many customers look at[online reviews](https://www.thryv.com/blog/social-proof-stacking-for-small-business/) to see what others have experienced.


Your reputation can help turn an interested shopper into a paying customer.

### 5. Reach Customers with Personalized Email and Text Campaigns


Social media helps customers discover your business, but email and text marketing give you another way to stay connected with people who already know you.


Rather than sending the same promotion to everyone, tailor your messages based on customer interests, past purchases, or engagement.


Here are a few ways to use email and text marketing during the holidays:


- **Announce your Small Business Saturday promotions:** Give customers an early look at upcoming deals, events, or seasonal packages.


- **Send personalized recommendations:** Highlight products or services based on what customers have previously purchased or shown interest in.


- **Share timely reminders:** Send a reminder about an upcoming event, limited-time offer or approaching holiday deadline.


- **Promote gift cards and seasonal services:** Reach customers who may still be looking for convenient gift ideas.


- **Thank customers after their purchase:** Follow up with a thank-you message and invite them to return.


A[simple holiday email campaign](https://www.thryv.com/blog/7-ways-small-business-marketing-software-can-help-you-automate-the-holidays/) could include three messages:


1. **The announcement:** Introduce your Small Business Saturday promotion and explain what customers can expect.


1. **The reminder:** Send a follow-up a few days before the event with the most important details.


1. **The follow-up:** Thank customers for supporting your business and share another reason to return.


Text messages work especially well for timely updates, appointment reminders and last-minute offers. Just make sure customers have opted in to receive marketing texts and that your messages follow applicable requirements.


Keep your messaging helpful and personal. Customers are more likely to engage when your emails and texts feel like useful recommendations rather than another holiday sales pitch.

### 6. Make It Easy for Customers to Buy, Book or Contact You


Getting customers interested in your business is only half the battle. You also need to make it easy for them to take the next step.


If someone finds your holiday promotion but can’t figure out how to book an appointment, make a purchase, or contact you, you could lose the opportunity.


Review your customer experience before Small Business Saturday and look for ways to remove unnecessary steps.


Start with these improvements:


- **Make your website mobile-friendly:** Ensure your website loads quickly, displays properly on mobile devices, and makes important information easy to find.


- **Use clear calls to action:** Add buttons such as “Shop Now,” “Book an Appointment,” “Get a Quote,” or “Call Today.”


- **Simplify online booking:** Let customers view available appointments and schedule services without having to call.


- **Make payment convenient:** Offer straightforward payment options and explain any deposits, fees, or purchasing requirements upfront.


- **Keep contact information visible:** Make your phone number, business hours, address, and service areas easy to find.


- **Respond to inquiries quickly:** Customers may be comparing multiple businesses, so timely responses can make a difference.


Think about the entire customer journey, from discovering your business to completing a purchase or booking. The fewer obstacles customers encounter, the easier it is for them to choose you.

### 7. Turn Small Business Saturday Shoppers Into Repeat Customers


Small Business Saturday shouldn’t be the end of your holiday marketing strategy. It’s an opportunity to introduce your business to new customers and give them a reason to come back.


Once the event is over, focus on keeping those relationships going throughout the holiday season and into the new year.


Here are a few ways to maintain momentum:


- **Send a thank-you message:** Show customers you appreciate their support and encourage them to stay connected.


- **Share upcoming promotions:** Give customers a preview of holiday specials, new products or seasonal services.


- **Encourage repeat purchases:** Offer a returning-customer incentive or early access to upcoming promotions.


- **Request customer feedback:** Use reviews and feedback to understand what customers enjoyed and where you can improve.


- **Stay active on social media:** Share event photos, customer stories and behind-the-scenes content to keep your business top of mind.


- **Reconnect with interested customers:** Follow up with people who requested information or showed interest but didn’t make a purchase.


You can also use the information you gather from your holiday campaigns to improve future marketing efforts. Look at which promotions attracted the most interest, which channels generated engagement, and which offers resulted in the most sales or bookings.


The more you understand what your customers respond to, the easier it becomes to create marketing that brings them back.

###

###
